title: 赠卫八处士
titleEn: For Wei the Eighth, a Recluse
author: 杜甫
intro: Twenty years after they last met, Du Fu turns up at an old friend’s door in wartime: the friend now has a house full of children, they eat spring chives cut in the rain and drink cup after cup — knowing tomorrow mountains will part them again.
analysis: 这首诗写一次战乱中的重逢。杜甫和老朋友卫八已经二十年没见面了，一天晚上突然在他家相聚。开头就是感叹：人生中朋友常常见不到面，就像参星和商星，一个升起另一个就落下。今晚是怎样难得的夜晚啊，我们竟能在同一盏灯下！接着说两人头发都白了，打听旧友，一半已经去世，惊叫起来，心里发热。二十年前分别时你还没结婚，现在儿女已经一大群，他们恭敬地向我问好，问我从哪里来。话还没说完，主人就催孩子们摆上了酒菜：雨夜里剪来的春韭，刚煮好的掺着黄米的饭。主人说见面太难了，一口气敬了十杯，我也没醉，因为感动于你的老交情。最后两句：明天我们又要被山岳隔开，世上的事，两个人都茫然不知了。全诗像讲故事，语言朴素，细节真实，把乱世中友情的珍贵和人生的无常写得非常动人。
analysisEn: This poem records a reunion in wartime. Du Fu and his old friend Wei had not met for twenty years when, one evening, he found himself at Wei’s house. It opens with a sigh: in life, friends often never meet, like the stars Shen and Shang — when one rises, the other has set. What a night this is, that we share the light of the same lamp! Both of them are grey now; asking after old friends, they find half are dead, and they cry out in shock, hearts burning. Twenty years ago Wei wasn’t married; now he has a crowd of children, who greet their father’s friend politely and ask where he has come from. Before the questions are finished, Wei sends the children to lay out wine and food: spring chives cut in the night rain, freshly cooked rice mixed with yellow millet. The host says meetings are hard to come by and toasts ten cups in a row; Du Fu doesn’t get drunk, moved by the warmth of an old friendship. The ending: tomorrow mountains will stand between us, and neither of us knows what the world will bring. Told like a story, in plain words and with true-to-life details, the poem shows how precious friendship is in troubled times, and how uncertain life can be.
background: Du Fu (712–770) wrote this in spring 759, during the An Lushan Rebellion, on his way back to his post in Huazhou. Nothing is known of Wei the Eighth beyond this poem; “the Eighth” is his rank among his brothers and cousins, and a 处士 is a man of learning who never took office.
pronunciation: 处士 chǔ shì；参与商 shēn（参星，不读 cān）；少壮 shào；半为鬼 wéi；载 zǎi；重上 chóng；成行 háng（成排）；父执 zhí；新炊间黄粱 jiàn（掺杂，不读 jiān）；一举累十觞 lěi（接连）；觞 shāng。
version: 采用《全唐诗》文本。“问答乃未已”，《唐诗三百首》等本作“问答未及已”；“驱儿罗酒浆”，有的选本作“儿女罗酒浆”；“剪春韭”的“剪”，古本作“翦”（同义），意思都相同。

lines.lit: In life, people do not get to meet;
lines.en: In this life, friends so seldom meet —

lines.lit: often they are like the stars Shen and Shang.
lines.en: like the two stars that never share the sky.

lines.lit: Tonight — what a night it is,
lines.en: What night is this, of all nights,

lines.lit: that we share this lamp and candlelight.
lines.en: that we sit in the same lamplight?

lines.lit: How long can youth and strength last?
lines.en: How long were we ever young?

lines.lit: The hair at our temples has each turned grey.
lines.en: Now both of us are grey.

lines.lit: Asking after old friends, half have become ghosts;
lines.en: We ask after old friends — half are dead;

lines.lit: crying out in shock, our insides burn.
lines.en: we cry out, and something burns inside.

lines.lit: How could I know that after twenty years
lines.en: Who knew that after twenty years

lines.lit: I would again climb into your hall, good sir?
lines.en: I would stand in your hall again?

lines.lit: When we parted before, you were not yet married;
lines.en: When we parted, you had no wife;

lines.lit: suddenly your sons and daughters stand in a row.
lines.en: now, all at once, a row of children.

lines.lit: Cheerfully they honour their father’s friend,
lines.en: They greet their father’s friend with smiles

lines.lit: asking me from what place I have come.
lines.en: and ask me where I’ve come from.

lines.lit: Before the questions and answers are over,
lines.en: Before the questions are done,

lines.lit: he sends his children to set out wine and drinks.
lines.en: he sends the children to lay out the wine.

lines.lit: In the night rain, spring chives are cut;
lines.en: Spring chives cut in the night rain,

lines.lit: freshly cooked rice is mixed with yellow millet.
lines.en: rice fresh from the pot, mixed with golden millet.

lines.lit: The host says meeting is hard;
lines.en: “Meetings are hard to come by,” says my host,

lines.lit: at one go he drinks ten cups in a row.
lines.en: and drinks ten cups straight off.

lines.lit: Ten cups, and still I am not drunk —
lines.en: Ten cups, and I am not drunk,

lines.lit: moved by your long friendship of old.
lines.en: so moved by your faithful old friendship.

lines.lit: Tomorrow, mountains will separate us;
lines.en: Tomorrow, mountains will lie between us,

lines.lit: the affairs of the world — both of us lost in the vastness.
lines.en: and neither of us knows what the world will bring.

words.en: a scholar who never took office

words.note: 两颗星此出彼没，永不同时出现，比喻难以相见。今天说“参商”。

words.en: what night is tonight — what a rare night
words.note: 今天仍用来表示惊喜，如“不知今夕何夕”。
现代汉语“苍老”“白发苍苍”。

words.en: to urge, send (someone to do something)
words.note: 古义“催促、使唤”；今天“驱赶”“驱车”。
现代汉语“连篇累牍”“累计”。
生僻字，见于成语“曲水流觞”。
古义“老交情”，今天“故意”是“有意地”，完全不同。

imagery.name: 星
imagery.zh: 参星和商星永不同时出现，比喻朋友分隔两地、难以相见。
imagery.en: The stars Shen and Shang never appear together — friends kept apart, unable to meet.

imagery.name: 烛
imagery.zh: 两人“共此灯烛光”，一盏灯照着难得的团聚，温暖而短暂。
imagery.en: Sharing one lamp’s light — a warm, brief circle around a rare reunion.

imagery.name: 酒
imagery.zh: 主人连敬十杯，酒里是二十年的情谊，也是对明天分别的不舍。
imagery.en: Ten cups in a row hold twenty years of friendship — and dread of tomorrow’s parting.
